headline.title: Pre-season: cold nights ahead.
headline.text: 5 of the 31 resorts close to opening get nights cold enough to make snow, mostly in Western Maine and White Mountains. Killington typically opens first, around Nov 8.

BTV.excerpt:
Near record high temperatures are expected today with mostly sunny conditions and limited, localized fire weather concerns.
Showers are expected on Thursday and possibly linger into Thursday night, then mainly dry weather will follow for Friday. No impactful weather is expected.
Periodic showers are possible over the weekend into early next week.

ALY.excerpt:
) Above normal temperatures and dry weather is expected today.
) A cold front will bring widespread beneficial rain showers Thursday, followed by additional chances for rain Fri into Saturday with the greatest probabilities south and east of the Capital District.

GYX.excerpt:
Warming peaks today with temperatures challenging records.
A widespread soaking rainfall is possible for the late week into the weekend along a slow moving frontal boundary.

BUF.excerpt:
) Near record warmth today with dry weather continuing through late afternoon.
) Showers return tonight, with unsettled weather and cooler temperatures lasting through next weekend.

PHI.excerpt:
No significant weather through today.
A slow moving cold front approaches the area Thursday night into Friday bringing the potential for heavy rain to portions of the area.

CTP.excerpt:
) Unseasonably mild through Friday with 2.5 weeks-long dry spell coming to an end overnight into Thursday
) Trending cooler this weekend with light rain downwind of Lake Erie

RLX.excerpt:
) A cold front brings showers and possible thunderstorms for Wednesday into Thursday.
) Cooler temperatures in store this weekend into the next work week with frost/freeze conditions looking probable.

writeups.name: Vermont
writeups.title: Quiet and mild.
paras: Next two days: summit temperatures from {{t:46}} to {{t:64}}, with rain at times.
Killington usually opens first here, around Nov 8. Jay Peak gets the most hours cold enough to make snow this week (about 11).
Trend: totals have come down since yesterday.
NWS Burlington forecasters, Wednesday 6:22 AM: "Near record high temperatures are expected today with mostly sunny conditions and limited, localized fire weather concerns."
writeups.outlook: Days 8 to 14: NOAA's outlook leans slightly warmer than normal and slightly drier than normal.
